title: Why consensus needs a majority
purpose: Explore why Raft waits for a majority, what goes wrong without it, and how cluster size changes the failures it survives.
summary: A short deck asks why Raft waits for a majority. The main path compares waiting for all servers, one server and a majority. Two deep dives show split brain without a majority rule and how many failures clusters of three to seven servers tolerate.
explanation: A majority is the smallest group that any other majority must overlap, which is what keeps two leaders from deciding different histories.

learning_check.question: How many failed servers can a cluster of four tolerate, and why not two?
learning_check.answer: One. A majority of four is three, so with two failures only two servers remain, which is not a majority.

slides.heading: Why wait for a majority?
slides.notes: Ask the learner what would go wrong with fewer or more acknowledgments.

slides.heading: Three ways to acknowledge a write
slides.notes: Reveal the options one at a time and ask which survives a crash and stays available.

items: Wait for all: one crash blocks every write
Wait for one: a crash can lose the write
Wait for a majority: survives crashes and stays safe

slides.heading: Majorities always overlap
slides.notes: Two majorities of five share at least one server, so a new leader always meets a server with the committed entries.

slides.heading: The trade-off
slides.notes: Raft chooses safety: without a majority it stops instead of risking two different histories.

visual.verdict: Consistency over availability during a partition.

slides.heading: A partition splits the cluster
slides.notes: If each side could elect a leader with any number of votes, both sides would accept different writes.

visual.verdict: Two histories: which x is true?

slides.heading: The majority rule prevents it
slides.notes: With the majority rule only side B, with three of five servers, can elect a leader, so only one history exists.

items: Side A has 2 of 5 votes: no leader
Side B has 3 of 5 votes: S3 leads

slides.heading: Failures each size survives
slides.notes: A cluster of n servers survives floor of (n minus 1) over 2 failures; adding a fourth server adds no tolerance.
